conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: City Lights
style.description: An invented city skyline at blue hour seen across water: layered rows of towers and mid-rise blocks in deep indigo with thousands of warm lit windows, rooftop beacons, a deck-arch bridge with moving headlights, a lamplit quay road, reflections shimmering and smearing on the water, and a gradient dusk sky with a last band of orange and the first stars. Windows are pixels, as a pure function of time: every facade is a window grid whose on/off/colour comes from a THREE-free plan — windows come on in seeded waves as dusk deepens, then organise into information: a row of towers becomes a bar chart (lit height = value, LED number signs on the roofs), one tower fills floor by floor like a progress bar, a wide block spells a word like a dot-matrix display, a heartbeat pulse runs across the skyline, and floors go dark one by one for a countdown. Traffic streams as moving dashes at planned densities, and the water repeats it all, smeared.
motion: Windows switch on in seeded waves as dusk deepens: each window has a planned on-time (a west-to-east wave + floor + jitter), some never light, a few flick off and back on later.
Programs take a building's windows over one by one (a staggered cascade, ~0.5 s), so the skyline visibly ORGANISES into information instead of cross-fading.
Bar chart: lit floors rise to value/max x floors with an eased count; the LED roof sign counts up with it. Fill: windows light in reading order, floor by floor, the head window flashing.
Word/icon: a 5x7 dot-matrix bitmap is wiped onto a wide block column by column; every other window on that face goes dark.

Heartbeat: a lub-dub pair of light fronts runs across the whole skyline (every window near the front brightens and whitens, even dark ones). Countdown: floors go dark from the top in steps while the roof sign shows the digit.
Traffic: head- and tail-light dashes stream along the bridge and quay at planned densities; the water re-renders everything mirrored and smears it into shimmering vertical streaks.

notes.sample: Bar values (38, 61, 47, 82, 70 of 100) and the 75 % fill are SAMPLE DATA, tagged on screen.
